title: Finite embedded blowup diagrams and their canonical smooth comparisons
statement: Let $n\in\mathbf N$. A finite embedded blowup diagram consists of functors $P,X:[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}$ [def-pc-scheme], a natural transformation $i:X\to P$ whose components are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaves $I_j$ on $P_j$ [pqf-def-coherent] for $j<n$. It includes isomorphisms $P_{j+1}\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{I_j}P_j$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] and $X_{j+1}\cong I_j.\operatorname{strictTransform}(i_j)$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], commuting with the transition maps and inclusions. No regularity, reducedness, nonempty-center or contraction requirement is imposed. A smooth comparison $E\to D$ consists of natural transformations on ambient and intrinsic functors, commuting with inclusions, whose levelwise intrinsic squares and successive ambient squares are cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its ambient maps are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] (hence flat), its center ideals are exactly the extensions [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and, under the stage isomorphisms, its ambient next-stage maps are the canonical flat blowup comparisons [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] followed by projection. Every stage and center is retained, including identity stages and unit ideals.
